page.layout: One page of text. Above the text, a decorative headpiece. Below it, the heading, then one verse stanza, the poet's name, a gathering mark, and a woodcut ornament in the lower left. No margin notes.

main_text.head: I. JACOMOTO SUO.
main_text.p: {D}CONQUERERIS, quærisque tibi cur carmina pauca Donarim, ô animæ pars, Jacomote, meæ. In prōptu causa est: Solymæ dum funera defles AnathotI quondam voce notata senis: Sic mea flebilibus pulsasti pectora dictis, Ut mens, lingua, manus dicere plura negent. Luxisti primus, quia me lugere volebas. A lugente putas carmina posse cani?

page.notes: The opening C of CONQUERERIS is a large decorative initial and is joined to the word. The reading "defles" is a close reading of the scan and could also be "deßes" or similar. "mens" in line 6 looks like "maens" or "mœns"; I read it as "mens" but it is doubtful. "AnathotI" ends in a capital I as printed. The "prōptu" abbreviation is shown with a macron over the o. The headpiece and the woodcut ornament below the text are not transcribed. Faint show-through of the reverse page and a faint "AD" at the lower left are not printed text on this page.
